clue.text: Laura is upset, in part, by deliverance from religion

indicators.note: in tells us the shuffled letters go inside the word for part

parts.note: a section is a part of something

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of Laura is are rearranged

explanation.surface: Laura, somewhat distressed, has been released from her religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laura is upset' reads as a distressed woman; 'upset' is the anagram signal and 'part' supplies the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something secular frees it from religious control, which is what deliverance from religion describes.

clue.text: Advertisements carried by food tables

parts.note: a sandwich is a common item of food
boards are tables, as in 'bed and board' or a festive board

explanation.surface: Adverts are carried by tables laden with food.
explanation.walkthrough: A sandwich board is a pair of hinged advertising placards worn front and back by a person walking the streets.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandwich-board placards are advertisements literally carried about on a person's body.

clue.text: Girl with a grinder in a state

indicators.note: in tells us the grinding device and the article sit inside the state's letters

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California
a mill is a machine that grinds grain or coffee

explanation.surface: A young woman with a coffee grinder is in one of the US states.
explanation.definitionFit: Camilla is a woman's given name, so it serves as an example of a girl's name.

clue.text: I don't have to listen to article about rip-off

indicators.note: about tells us the newspaper piece goes round the other letters

parts.note: a leader is a newspaper's editorial article

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or awry, so the letters of rip are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that they needn't listen to a piece about a swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rip-off' looks like one word for a swindle; it splits into fodder and the anagram signal 'off'. A leader is the British term for a newspaper editorial.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who reads lips understands speech by watching mouths, so hearing is unnecessary for them.

clue.text: Make new disposition, almost completely, of king on back row

indicators.note: almost completely means a little is left off the end of the word for reorganising

parts.note: to rearrange is to set things out in a new disposition
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Instructions to reorganise a king's position on the back row, as in chess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make new disposition' looks like the definition, but it is the word to be trimmed; the definition is 'back row' at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: In a military formation the rear rank is the hindmost line of soldiers, i.e. the back row.

clue.text: Writer of 14 disposition

indicators.note: disposition means an arrangement, so the letters of that name are set out anew

parts.note: the answer to 14 across is a man's name meaning bird plus street

explanation.surface: The author who wrote with a particular temperament, as described at clue 14.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' rearranges ERNEST, the answer to 14 across, into the writer's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne was an eighteenth-century novelist, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Hornblower's sweetheart?

parts.note: a term of endearment for a girlfriend, which also describes what someone blowing a horn produces

explanation.surface: Asks who the beloved of a horn player might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toots' is an American pet name for a woman; a horn-blower also produces short blasts of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Toots is slang for a sweetheart or darling, and short horn blasts share the word.

clue.text: Conceal lines about c-crossword element being incomplete

indicators.note: about tells us the poem goes round the other letters

parts.note: an ode is a poem, a set of lines of verse
the stammered c- gives the letter C

indicators.note: being incomplete means the word for a crossword element loses its last letter

parts.note: every crossword is made of clues

explanation.surface: Hide some lines of verse about a stammered, unfinished part of a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammered 'c-' is a single letter piece, not part of the crossword element.
explanation.definitionFit: To occlude is to block or shut off from view, which is to conceal.

clue.text: South coast resort proclaimed with love at sunrise?

indicators.note: proclaimed means said out loud, so the resort's name is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast
dearly means with love or affection

explanation.surface: A south-coast seaside town spoken of with affection at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON said aloud gives BRIGHT AN; joined to DEARLY it splits as BRIGHT AND EARLY. Brighton is a well-known seaside resort in Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: Up bright and early means up very early in the morning, around sunrise.

clue.text: Christen South American river in brass at the door

parts.note: to christen someone is to name them
the River Plate is the estuary between Argentina and Uruguay

explanation.surface: Instructions to baptise a South American river in a brass ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A nameplate is a plaque, often of brass, fixed by a front door to show who lives there.

clue.text: Writer taking very great pains to hide being very angry

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, i.e. very great

indicators.note: to hide signals that one word is concealed inside another

parts.note: taking pains means taking care
wild means furious, very angry

explanation.surface: An author going to enormous trouble to conceal his fury.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a British clothing-size label; 'taking' and 'being' just join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish playwright and wit who wrote The Importance of Being Earnest was a celebrated writer.

clue.text: See 10
Tears when food returns to north German town

parts.note: tears (as a verb) means rends, rips apart

indicators.note: returns means the word for food is read backwards

parts.note: grub is informal for food

explanation.surface: Weeping when food is sent back, in a northern German town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns GRUB into BURG. 'Tears' is the verb (pronounced tares), not weeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendsburg is a town on the Kiel Canal in Schleswig-Holstein, northern Germany.

clue.text: Keep hold when about to put on pebbledash, say

indicators.note: about tells us the word for holding fast goes round the other letters

parts.note: to cling is to keep hold of something
to add is to put on, as in adding weight

explanation.surface: Grip tightly when about to apply a rough render to a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Pebbledash is a British exterior wall finish of render studded with small stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Pebbledash is one kind of covering applied to the outside of a building, an example of cladding.

clue.text: Bird on street of consequence for 10 11

parts.note: an erne is a sea eagle, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A bird on a street of some importance, connected with a famous writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the title The Importance of Being Earnest by Oscar Wilde: the name sounds like the adjective for serious, so it is the thing of importance.
explanation.definitionFit: In the play's title, being a man of this name is what carries importance, so it is the name of consequence.

clue.text: Metallic element from old show for old king shedding old city

parts.note: a raree show was an old travelling peep show

indicators.note: shedding means the city's letters are dropped from the king's name

parts.note: King Arthur is the legendary ancient British king
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A metal emerges from a vintage entertainment staged for a former monarch who has lost an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shedding' takes UR out of ARTHUR, leaving ARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: The rare earths are a group of metallic chemical elements, the lanthanides, so one is a metallic element.

clue.text: Swinger to finish posh in appropriately vocal fruit?

indicators.note: in tells us the two pieces go inside the fruit

parts.note: a posh voice is called plummy, so the plum is the fruit that suits speaking posh
end means finish
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: Someone who swings, ending up posh inside a fruit with a voice to match.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'plummy' voice is a rich upper-class British accent, so the plum is the apt fruit for posh speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendulum is a weight that swings to and fro, so it is a swinger.

clue.text: Film actor's low standard painting?

parts.note: bog-standard means ordinary, of low standard
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: Asks whether a film star's poor-quality picture is meant.
explanation.walkthrough: Bog-standard is British slang for plain or mediocre; bog is also slang for a lavatory, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Humphrey Bogart was a Hollywood star of Casablanca, a famous film actor.

clue.text: Time off for transmission without pay, possibly

indicators.note: without means outside, so the transmission word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a vehicle's gear is part of its transmission

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of pay are arranged another way

explanation.surface: Time away from work is a gearbox fault, without pay perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense of outside, not lacking, signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap year is a year taken off between school and university or work.

clue.text: Success over planet to become less substantial?

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the word for success goes round the planet

parts.note: a win is a success
Earth is our planet

explanation.surface: Triumph across the world to become thinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition's question mark hints at the literal sense of clothing becoming threadbare.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear thin is to become weaker or flimsier, less substantial, as an excuse does.

clue.text: History of the weird banshee

indicators.note: weird means strange or odd, so the letters of banshee are jumbled

explanation.surface: An account of the past of an eerie wailing spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: A banshee is a wailing female spirit of Irish folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is 'history' is finished and past their best, which is what a has-been is.

clue.text: Mollycoddle agent — plan coming up

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent, a representative
a map is a plan

explanation.surface: An agent with a plan rising to fuss over someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns REPMAP into PAMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: To mollycoddle someone is to indulge and over-protect them, a synonym for pamper.

clue.text: 21s topped with additional sign

indicators.note: topped means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: the answer to 21 down made plural, as a verb meaning indulges
and means plus, in addition

explanation.surface: Indulgences beheaded and an extra symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' removes the P from PAMPERS, leaving AMPERS.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampersand is the printed sign & standing for 'and'.

clue.text: Avuncular black man — there must be some

indicators.note: there must be some of the letters of these words, so part of them is taken

explanation.surface: Refers to a fatherly old figure of whom there must be a little.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Remus is the elderly black storyteller of Joel Chandler Harris's tales, hence 'avuncular'.
explanation.definitionFit: Remus is the name of the narrator known as Uncle Remus, so the uncle-like black man.

clue.text: Girl will be first in otherwise

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for first goes inside the word for otherwise

parts.note: else means otherwise
I is the Roman numeral one, first

explanation.surface: A girl will come first or else.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsie is a girl's given name, an example of a girl.

clue.text: Fancy 250,000 sheets?

parts.note: a ream is 500 sheets, and D is the Roman 500, so 500 reams make 250,000 sheets
a ream of paper is 500 sheets

explanation.surface: Imagine an enormous quantity of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: D (500) times REAM (500 sheets) gives 250,000 sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is an imagined notion or wish, a synonym for a dream.

clue.text: Endangered beast takes fruit round world, including US city

indicators.note: round means the fruit encloses the other letters

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: including tells us the city sits inside the word for world

parts.note: an orb is a globe, a world
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A threatened animal carries fruit around the globe, with an American city on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' joins the beast to its wordplay; there are two containers nested, one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar bears are threatened by shrinking Arctic sea ice, an endangered beast.

clue.text: Is worker on cars in essay by 5?

indicators.note: in tells us the pieces go inside the word for essay

parts.note: an essay is an attempt, a try

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the worker follows the cars

parts.note: taken as written
trams are tramcars
a hand is a worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: Asks whether a tram worker features in an essay by a certain writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 down is STERNE, whose novel Tristram Shandy is defined here as a work by him.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristram Shandy is the novel by Laurence Sterne, the answer to 5 down, so it is a work by him.
